scope: Production dry renderer. Frozen scene; fluid simulation, water rendering and browser presentation excluded. GI disabled in both backends. Same 31 authored lights and full-resolution material shading in baseline comparisons. GPU frame-span medians, 16 measured frames per arm across forward/reverse blocks, four warmups per block; same orbit sequence.
recommendation: Raster shadows plus screen-space AO have the strongest direct-lighting performance potential for this mostly static, many-light scene. Cache point-light visibility in world space. Cones are worth retaining for optional indirect lighting, not as the fix for these direct-shadow traversals.
findings: Camera motion invalidates exact dry-frame/receiver reuse; static world geometry and lights do not themselves change.
Raster at 800x460: 402.46 ms baseline, 7.60 ms with shadows disabled, 7.08 ms with both AO and shadows disabled. Disabling AO alone does not improve the frame.

Raster baseline compute medians: reduced all-light visibility 229.57 ms; exact visibility exceptions 168.10 ms; half-resolution sun visibility and horizon AO 0.98 ms. Per-pass medians need not sum to frame median.

Tokyo publishes 28 point lights, two spotlights and one directional light. All local lights have unlimited radiance range. The existing cached maps support the sun and up to four finite-range spots, so none of these local lights qualify.

Imported sampled receivers take drySampledSurfaceVisibility before the generic cone shortcut. Cone mode therefore still executes expensive native primitive and voxel shadow traversal. Its compact prepass also stores only eight light visibilities; Tokyo has 31 lights.
At 200x115, raster takes 250.68 ms and cones 317.33 ms. Shadows-off controls are 2.03 and 3.15 ms respectively. These are backend costs at this resolution, not interactive FPS.
Smooth Tokyo surfaces cannot use the current cone lattice visibility cache: eligibility requires flatVoxelNormals.

Cones at 800x460 and 400x230 produced missing timestamps and all-zero readbacks after expensive frames. Quarter-scale joint-bilateral cones at 800x460 also failed the nonzero-frame check. These runs are excluded; this investigation does not establish the cause of the backend failure.

kept: Headless imported-asset registration before world construction
Repeatable moving-camera/stationary lighting ablations, captures, invalid-readback and missing-timestamp rejection
World-space point-light cube faces packed into an atlas; unlimited-spot projection bounds independent of radiance range
Covered-light visibility specialization retains exact fallback for unsupported live publications
Batch all cube faces sharing a physical atlas layer into one render pass
Single-material sampled-surface fast path, shared visibility coordinates, and fully occluded BRDF rejection
Conservative reflection depth bounds with exact per-pixel intersections
Texture gathers for shadow PCF and weighted visibility, preserving border clamping

Pack three scalar opaque-shadow samples per RGB10 word only under complete map coverage, with water-shadow and unsupported-light fallback to RGB. Same ten-bit quantization, one third of atlas storage (33 layers to 11 in Tokyo).

Validate imported-camera occupancy against the native source field before withholding raster geometry. Coarse proxy occupancy incorrectly classified air as solid, forcing expensive full-scene tracing and producing phantom surfaces. Unknown, sculpted and genuinely interior points retain the fallback.

Cached mapped shadows return immediately when there are no rigid bodies, omitting biased-ray and domain-boundary setup; finite local body rays avoid directional scene-boundary intersection. GPU tests cover absent bodies, finite/directional blockers, shadow strength, backfaces and shadows disabled.

Bodyless, water-shadow-free unlimited point-map queries bypass normalized light sampling. Finite lights, unsupported maps and grazing angles retain the full evaluator.8192 GPU differential cases passed;14 GPU tests passed across producer, packed visibility, optical frame and body-correction paths.

The direct BRDF accepts the unit light direction already produced by the light sampler; Schlick uses three multiplications for its fixed fifth power. Generic unnormalized callers retain their normalizing wrapper.4096 unit-light BRDF cases and65536 Fresnel cases passed, plus existing GPU optical/light-budget tests. Reference capture changed19 channels by1/255.
discarded: Clip native shadow marches to leaf AABBs: 397.41 vs 402.46 ms baseline, too small/noisy to justify changed acceptance near surfaces (33/17 image channel bytes differed in stationary/orbit captures).
Invocation-private last-blocker hint: slower than baseline despite re-intersecting every ray; removed.
Packing four RGB10 light samples into rgba32uint texels: full-resolution frame median 19.07 vs 19.33 ms; insufficient gain to retain the additional cache/layout complexity.
Fixed interactive pixel budget removed after the user requested full-resolution rendering.
Hardware texture filtering passed GPU parity tests but full-resolution orbit remained 18.22 ms vs18.29 ms; reverted as no measurable benefit.
Direct per-pixel shadow map reads instead of the visibility atlas regressed full-resolution orbit to31.06 ms; reverted.
Explicitly vectorized receiver-plane PCF increased AO and shadow filtering cost; restored the original four-texel loop.
Reusing reflection ray endpoints passed differential GPU tests but produced no measurable frame-time gain (14.94 vs 14.88 ms); reverted.
Early point-light backface rejection passed 4096 GPU parity cases, but did not improve complete-frame timing (14.81 ms orbit median vs 14.42 ms in the preceding longer run). Removed.
4x4 reflection bounds passed all six GPU checks but had mixed small timing changes (orbit14.68 vs14.48 ms, pan12.45 vs12.58 ms). Restored8x8 rather than retain an inconclusive tuning change.

Unbounded enclosing-native-primitive intersection as an upper-bound seed for fallback traversal: captures were unchanged, but added expensive queries and regressed pan max33.75 ms and wide-orbit max43.71 ms. Reverted; inspecting actual GPU occupancy classification instead.

implementationPlan.change: Add cached cubemap/atlas shadows for point lights, using camera-independent finest native caster geometry and existing scene geometry.
implementationPlan.reason: Removes native field traversal per visible receiver per point light. This is the dominant cost.
implementationPlan.constraints: Bound atlas memory and resolution; preserve an exact fallback for unsupported lights or incomplete maps; validate thin lantern/sign/cyclist occluders and cubemap seams.

implementationPlan.change: Support unlimited-range spotlights by deriving finite shadow-map coverage from scene bounds, independently of radiance attenuation.
implementationPlan.reason: The two practical spotlights currently miss the cached path solely because range_m is zero.
implementationPlan.constraints: Do not add a radiance cutoff or change the authored light intensity; fall back outside proven shadow-map coverage.

implementationPlan.change: Invalidate local maps on caster/light geometry changes, independently of camera motion; evaluate moving-body and fluid attenuation separately.
implementationPlan.reason: The authored Tokyo architecture, cyclist and fixtures are static; camera orbit should only pay map lookup costs.
implementationPlan.constraints: Preserve edits, light transforms, source publications, native asset changes and live water correctness.

implementationPlan.change: Retain horizon AO; evaluate cones separately for GI once direct shadows are cheap. Run matched moving-camera captures at 800x460 and the requested full 1200x800 resolution.
implementationPlan.reason: AO is already inexpensive; replacing it does not address the observed bottleneck.
implementationPlan.constraints: Preserve full resolution; report complete-frame medians, tails and over-budget counts; do not equate GPU time to verified browser FPS.
implementationPlan.status: Implementation and native GPU validation complete; strict no-drop browser 60 fps remains unverified (adapter unavailable, one 16.71 ms GPU outlier across 6000 moving frames).

resolutionPolicy: Preserve full resolution. No scene pixel budget, adaptive resolution or camera-motion quality reduction is retained.
implementationStatus: Full 1200x800 resolution retained. Batched empty-tile reflection traversal retained; cached zero-visibility skip rejected as slower. Two complete-frame runs: 5999/6000 moving GPU frames within 16.67 ms; one repeat orbit frame measured 16.71168 ms. The original inside-solid pan/zoom spikes are removed (max 14.155776 ms in both retained runs). Typecheck, 1343 unit tests (204 GPU-dependent skips), six GPU reflection tests and 8192 ray comparisons passed. Browser WebGPU adapter unavailable, so strict browser 60 fps is not established.

notes: Full-renderer studies include water, reflections and final display rendering with simulation paused; they do not establish live fluid solver throughput or browser requestAnimationFrame FPS.
The existing Chrome tab could not obtain a WebGPU adapter, including after reload. Native Dawn Metal remains usable.

Completed geometry remains cached when the camera temporarily withholds its draw inside solids; this avoids unnecessary mesh emission and shadow passes. Material single-ID filtering, per-pixel atlas addresses, zero-visibility BRDF rejection and squared reflection-depth comparisons are retained. No presentation-resolution cap is used.

Conservative 8×8 reflection depth bounds preserve full-resolution pixel intersections. GPU differential tests cover 4,096 ray comparisons including two viewport sizes, empty-frame updates and mismatched raster extents. Full Tokyo image differs by only four 8-bit channels, each by one level, from the ungated pixel walk.

Empty reflection tiles previously advanced through up to 16 individual pixel-boundary branches. Batched axis crossing counts retain repeated f32 additions and exact corner behavior, avoiding those branches. Full-resolution GPU comparison now covers 8192 rays including nearly axis-aligned rays. Three camera-inside-solid captures are byte-identical; orbit probes differ by at most one 8-bit level in 13 channels. Temporary occupancy diagnostics and the rejected native intersection seed were removed.

A repeat of the retained batched-reflection implementation produced one isolated orbit frame at 16.71168 ms (frame 885), with neighboring frames at 12.5-13.4 ms. The raw span contains a 2.8 ms gap before rasterization, but its cause is not established. It remains counted as over budget; results do not discard outliers or equate GPU timing with browser frame pacing.
